messages.author: 4ce6c57a10fb76bf
messages.subject: Fitting of a time-varying coefficients model to a large set of sampling units
parts:
Hi all,

I'm pretty new to Stan, so I'm sure this would be a rather stupid question; I'm trying to fit a time series model to the growth (GWTH) of a set of individual trees (K=26) measured during N=16 years, accounting for the effects of herbivore browsing (gamma) on growth. My goal is to fit a time-varying coefficients model in which the effect of herbivores on each tree, as well as the stochastic terms sigma, vary across time according to random walks. I’m stuck in the specification of these parameters; I guess that the time-varying terms gamma and sigma should be specified as matrix[N,K], but I get a SYNTAX message error (“no matches for function name="add”). When I specify these parameters as constant, the model works pretty well. Can anyone help me and point to what I’m doing wrong? I paste below the minimal model I'm trying to fit, thank you very much in advance.

model<-'

data {

int<lower=0> N; // number of time steps, 16
int<lower=0> K; // number of trees, 26
matrix[N,K] RHG; //  matrix for RHGs
vector[N] herb; //  Leader browsing
}

parameters {
vector[K] rnd_slope; // intercepts         
matrix[N,K] gamma; // coefficient for herbivore
real<lower=0> sigma[N,K]; // stochastic effects
}

model {

for (n in 1:N)
  RHG[n] ~ normal(rnd_slope + gamma[n]*herb[n], sigma[n]);

for (n in 2:N)
  gamma[n] ~ dnorm(gamma[n-1], 1)

for (n in 2:N)
  sigma[n] ~ dnorm(sigma[n-1], 1)
                      
}'

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Fitting of a time-varying coefficients model to a large set of sampling units
parts:
You can use "gamma" as a parameter name --- there are no conflicts
with variables and function names, or we'd be in big trouble!

You have two problems due to treating Stan like R or JAGS/BUGS
(a not uncommon problem for new users):

1. you need semicolons at the end of every statement, and

2. you need to use our function names, e.g., "normal" rather than "dnorm".

It would be possible with some ugly index fiddling for vectorization
and changing basic types to make it faster (see the manual chapter on
arrays vs. matrices and the section on time series model in the regression
chapter), but I'd suggest getting it working first.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fitting of a time-varying coefficients model to a large set of sampling units
parts:
The error message is telling you that your problem is that
the sigma argument is a 2D array.

First off, the reason the patched version is "desperately slow"
is that you're oversampling:

// The following works, but is desperately slow:
// for (n in 1:N)
// for (k in 1:K)
// RHG[n] ~ normal(rnd_slope + gamma[n,k]*herb[n], sigma); you can change this:

That should presumably be RHG[n,k] ~ ...

As is, you're doing K times too much work here and also providing
the wrong distribution. Unfortunately, there's no way for us to
auto-detect this problem and allow vectorization.

To make things efficient, you need to rearrange your data.

The right thing to do differs as to whether N >> K or vice versa.
I'll just do it the easy way, including making the variable
declarations more efficient without changing how the I/O works (see
the chapter on arrays vs. matrices for details of why this is better):

vector[K] RHG[N]; // matrix for RHGs

vector[K] gamma[N]; // coefficient for herbivore

vector<lower=0>[K] sigma[N]; // stochastic effects
for (n in 1:N)

RHG[n] ~ normal(rnd_slope + gamma[n] * herb[n], sigma[n]);

This will work because

RHG[n] : vector[K]
rnd_slope : vector[K]
gamma[n] : vector[K]
herb[n] : real

If N >> K, it would make sense to transpose all this and vectorize
in a for (k in 1:K) loop, but I don't have the stamina to work it
all out for you.

- Bob
